html:
The Winged Victory of Samothrace is a marble statue of Nike, the Greek goddess of victory, made around 190 BCE. It is one of the masterpieces of Hellenistic sculpture and now stands at the top of a grand staircase in the Louvre in Paris.

The goddess is shown landing on the prow of a warship, her wings spread and her thin dress pressed against her body and rippling behind her in the sea wind. Her head and arms are lost. She stood in the Sanctuary of the Great Gods on the island of Samothrace in the north Aegean, set above a pool so that the ship seemed to float.

She was almost certainly put up to thank the gods for a victory at sea. The ship's base is made of grey marble from Rhodes, so many scholars link her to Rhodian sea victories of about 190 BCE over the Seleucid king Antiochus III, though this is not certain.

A French diplomat found her in pieces in 1863 and shipped her to Paris. Her right hand was found in 1950. Like the Colossus of Rhodes, she shows the bold, dramatic style of art after Alexander.
